content_of_post_to_comment: It’s true that there are lots of millionaires in America today. When the term “millionaire” entered English (1821), a million dollars was worth $30 million today. When I was born (1965), a million dollars was worth ten million dollars today. There are lots of millionaires today largely because it’s a lot easier to be a millionaire when the dollar is worth 1/10 of what it was worth 60 years ago. Maybe we need a new term to replace “millionaire”, something to indicate someone who has a million dollars in 1965 or 1821 dollars (ie, 10–40 million dollars).
